title: Trionic Array I
summary: Given an integer array of length n, determine if there exist indices 0 < p < q < n - 1 where the array segments nums[0...p], nums[p...q], and nums[q...n-1] are strictly increasing, strictly decreasing, and strictly increasing respectively.
statement: Given an integer array of length n, determine if there exist indices 0 < p < q < n - 1 where the array segments nums[0...p], nums[p...q], and nums[q...n-1] are strictly increasing, strictly decreasing, and strictly increasing respectively. Return true if the array meets these conditions, otherwise return false.
constraints: Split the complete array into three nonempty edge sequences: strictly increasing, then strictly decreasing, then strictly increasing.
The two turning indices must be internal.
Return whether such a split exists.
reference_solution:
def is_trionic_array(nums):
    i=1
    while i<len(nums) and nums[i]>nums[i-1]:i+=1
    if i==1 or i==len(nums) or nums[i]>=nums[i-1]:return False
    while i<len(nums) and nums[i]<nums[i-1]:i+=1
    if i==len(nums) or nums[i]<=nums[i-1]:return False
    while i<len(nums) and nums[i]>nums[i-1]:i+=1
    return i==len(nums)

hints: Consume the maximal initial strict rise.
Require it to be nonempty and followed by a strict fall.
Consume that fall, require a final rise, then consume it.
Success requires reaching the array end after all three nonempty phases.
